utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody and Ms. Regue. How are you this morning?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good. Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the sheet given to you now, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, the Prosecution would like to call witness M-019, Mr. Vehbi Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have a technical problem. We ask that we wait for five minutes or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Apparently there is a problem with interpretation from what I'm hearing. I don't know what that is yet.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is resolved now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For me, it's okay, sir. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. It's now coming through to me. I'm not sure where the problem is or whether it has been cured. I just heard that it was. But the sound it is now operational. Can you hear what is being said, translated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, I think you may proceed now, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Good morning, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, do you recall providing a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in February 2003?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting with a representative from the Registry who certified your statement in August 2006?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting with myself and other colleague in Ljuboten in April of this year and providing an additional brief statement?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to read both documents before coming here today?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, are you satisfied that its contents are correct and accurate?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender the 2003 statement and also the addendum of 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this pursuant to Rule 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The first statement is pursuant to Rule 92 bis, Your Honour. The second is an addendum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. They will received together as each part of the one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The statement will become P247.1 and the addendum will become Exhibit P247.2, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The witness, Mr. Bajrami, is an ethnic Albanian. He was born in Ljuboten where he was residing during the relevant time-period of the indictment. Between 10 to 11 August 2001 Mr. Bajrami heard shooting, shelling and a sniper shots directed at the village of Ljuboten. On 12 August 2001, members of the Macedonian armed forces entered Ljuboten. Soon after, Macedonian police, including members of the Lions, entered the yard of Adem Ametovski house in which basement the witness and a number of other men were sheltering. They were searched, forced to lie down, and beaten severely by the Macedonian police. The witness saw an armoured vehicle with an anti-aircraft heavy weapon mounted on the top. The men were ordered out to the main gate where they were again made to lie down. They were beaten and mistreated. And the witness heard the sound of constant intensive shooting around him. The witness's brother, Sulejman Bajrami was shot dead at this time. The men were forced to march to Brace's house. They were abused and mistreated whilst walking to Brace's house and on their arrival there. They were subsequently transported to Mirkovci police station where they were again beaten by policemen. The witness was forced to sign a statement declaring that was found in possession of fire-arms. Two days after, the witness was brought before a judge ever the Skopje Court and then taken to Sutka prison where he remained for approximately four months. Your Honours, I have binders for Your Honours and also for my learned friend, if the usher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I would like to call 65 ter 152. And, if possible, not shown outside the courtroom. It's tab 1 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the Macedonian version of the document on the right side of your screen?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you can please focus on the upper left corner, do you see Ministry of Interior of Republic of Macedonia, the first line?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we move three lines below, do you read police station Mirkovci, then Angel Petkovski, 14 August 2001, Skopje?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we move in the centre of the document, do you read the title, Official Note, number 1194, and then persons taken to court and handed over to investigative prison, Sutka?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we move a bit down, do you see five names?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see your name in the first bullet point?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Bajrami Vebi.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we read the paragraph below it says: "They were taken to the basic court in Skopje II where they were questioned by Judge Velce Pancevski with the decision number 436/01. The judge determined custody measure of 30 days to the above-mentioned persons, and after this they were handed over to commander Zivko in the investigative prison, Sutka." Do you read this, Mr. Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: On which side? On the right or on the left.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the counsel be asked to slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just the paragraph below the names.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: To the names.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Below the names.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, were these people with you in Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were these people taken together with you to Skopje Court and then to Sutka prison?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P248, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I would like to call Exhibit P00046, page 48. Tab 2 in the court binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, do you see the Macedonian version on the right side of your screen?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you could please look at the upper left corner, do you read Ministry of Interior, OVR-OOR Cair?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: On the right or on the left side, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: On the left side, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you read below: 12 August 2001, Skopje?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The numbers, do you see just below the numbers, 12 --

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, now yes. Yeah, 12, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If could you please read in the centre of the document in capital letters there is a title. It says "certificate on temporary seized possessions." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And then below it read: On day of 12 August 2001, at the police station Mirkovci from the person Bajrami Vebi and then we see some personal information of you. Your date of birth. And then just one line below it says: "Seized the following possessions in temporary "custody," and then we move to number 1, it says, one automatic rifle, Thomson, calibre 45, and 100 bullets?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So have you ever been in possession of this weapon and this ammunition, Mr. Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, I never had it. I have been living in Cair for 32 years and I never had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, if we could please scroll down the document so we can see the signature on the bottom left corner. Do you see a signature in the bottom left corner of the document, Mr. Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you sign this document voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No. I was forced. It was under duress. He told me if you don't sign it, I will put the Kalashnikov at your head.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: The police at Mirkovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I would like to move to Exhibit P46, pages 64 to 66. And with Your Honour's leave, I will work in hard copy due to the bad quality of the Macedonian version with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if could I have the usher's assistance in providing the witness with the Macedonian version. Also, in order to speed up the proceedings you will see that the numbered the paragraphs, the English and the Macedonian and also I highlighted what I'm going to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, if you could please look at the first page that you have in front of you. Do you see in the upper part, in the centre 14 August 2001 and then your name?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And then on the left, Skopje, Velce Pancevski?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, if you can move to the second page, also the second page in the English document. I'm going to read to you the first paragraph. It says: "It started at 1445 hours pursuant to Article 27, from ZKP and advise on the right to use his native language, the accused said that he speaks and understand Macedonian language. Also he said that he will give his statement in Macedonian language." Mr. Bajrami, did you state to the judge that you wish to give your statement in Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, No, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we move, please, to the second paragraph. I'm going to read it to you as well: "Pursuant to Article 210, Paragraph 2 from "ZKP the accused was informed that OJO Skopje sent a request for implementation of investigation and proposal to impose a detention" - then we see some numbers - "because of the well-based suspicion he committed a criminal act of terrorist." Mr. Bajrami, for the record, you ever commit an act of terrorist?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Never in my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Have you ever been a member of a terrorist group?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please move to the fourth paragraph. The highlighted sentence reads: "Although I was and I was beaten the police, I can give a statement, I want to speak."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, did you state to the judge that you had been beaten by the police?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: The police, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, if we can move to the seventh paragraph, the next highlighted sentence, Mr. Bajrami, it reads: "The accused stated I accept this attorney to represent me as my defence attorney." Mr. Bajrami, do you recall an attorney being present in the courtroom when you were in front of the judge?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No. I saw someone being there but nobody indicated to me that it was my lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you say to the judge that you accepted this person as your attorney?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we move to paragraph 9 in the English version we are already in the second page, still the first one in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I will read it to you Mr. Bajrami: "I have noticeable injuries on my face, in my [indiscernible], and my right eye is closed, I can see only through my left eye." Mr. Bajrami, is this is accurate description of the injuries that you were suffering that day?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Based on what you stated two paragraphs above, were these injuries a result of the police beatings?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Then if we move to paragraph 10 we can see Beqir Ramadani is my brother. Mr. Bajrami, is Beqir Ramadani your brother?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you ever that to the judge?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, if you could please look at the next page?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: It's the last page in the English version, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I will read to you the two lines which are highlighted: "We were beaten by the local residents while we walk." And then one line below it says "when I was brought in the police they did not beat me." Mr. Bajrami, did you say this to the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't understand. I'm not very clear. Can you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sure. In your statement that you allegedly gave to the judge it says: "We were beaten by the local residents while we walk." And then it says: "When I was brought in the police, they," meaning the police,"did not beat me." And my question was: " Did you stated this to the judge?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move to the bottom of the document just below the word "accuse."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, do you see a signature there?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Is this your signature, Mr. Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You did ask the witness about the document at tab 2. Do I correctly understand that's part of Exhibit P46? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could I please ask a clarification to the witness. Now reading the transcript, I'm not sure whether it came out clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, do you remember that you answer that you didn't state to the judge that you had been beaten by the local residents?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Also, you didn't say that when you were brought in the police, the police did not beat you?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because it's a fact that the police beat us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. Can I conclude from your answer that what is written in here is not correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: You mean here in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes. The two sentences that I just repeated to you.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: They are not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honours. Now I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm still tracking the exhibits. The document at tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That was a 65 ter number that we tendered today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You sought to tender it today that. That was -- and that's Exhibit P278 -- 248.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, 248. I was checking the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you move the -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bajrami. My name is Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague Mr. Guenael Mettraux, I appear for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Mr. Bajrami, as you have told my learned friend, you made a statement to an investigator of the OTP, and you gave addenda to that statement which were accepted today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were born in Ljuboten and you are the son of Aziz Bajrami; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There were ten children in your family, six brothers, you, and three sisters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: We are seven brothers, or used to be seven brothers, and three sisters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was precisely what I said. Counting you, there was seven brothers and three sisters.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: We used to be. We are no longer seven.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, there were two houses owned by your family in the village, an old one and a new one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we have two houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your father was a farmer, and your mother a housewife; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, only your sister Ramiza, who was married, was not living in the household with you while all the rest of you were still living together; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: That is not correct. Because my brother Rafiz was in Italy. Shefajet was in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your family had a modest lifestyle. One could say that life was difficult. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether it's correct that at that time you lived quite modestly in your family. You were not very well off; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: It is not correct. We were, I would say, living a normal life.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If your mother in her statement to the court in Skopje said that you lived with a quite modest lifestyle, that would not be quite correct, would it?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: We lived well, I would say. It was an average life. My mother now is dead. I don't know what she said in the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. When you were released from detention you made several statements to various international organisations. Would it be correct to say that you made your first statement on the 1st of January, 2002 to representatives of the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't remember. Maybe it's true, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You made another statement to the members of the International Committee of the Red Cross; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know. I have forgotten. Maybe it is, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you made a statement to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal on the 8th of February, 2003, you signed that statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, in 2003. On the 8th of February, yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You speak only Albanian and Macedonian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. But Macedonian I understand very little. I speak Albanian mostly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The statement you gave to investigators of the Tribunal is one that you signed in English, and it was interpreted to you, or translated to you into Albanian later on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, would it be true to say that in 2001, in view of your occupation and your age, you didn't have any special knowledge of the structure of the army and police of the Republic of Macedonia? Would that be true to say?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't understand what you are saying. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, Mr. Bajrami, is whether it's correct that you don't have any special knowledge of the structure of the army of the Republic of Macedonia and the structure of the police of the Republic of Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, but, again, I can't understand what you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you the following: Do you know what organs and units exist in the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: You mean that I served in or what? I was in the army, this is what you are asking me?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. What I'm asking you is whether you are aware of the structure, the competences, and the organs in the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Are you aware of this or not?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you don't know what the structure, responsibilities and powers are of individual organs within the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Again, I don't understand what is your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is whether you, Mr. Bajrami, are familiar with the way in which the police is organised; that is, the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Macedonia. Do you know what organs it consists of and what their competences are?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I fail to understand your point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll move on, and I'll put other questions to you which I hope you will understand. As a citizen of the Republic of Macedonia, you probably know that in the Republic of Macedonia it is judges, investigating judges in the courts who carry out investigations; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So you do not know who is in charge of conducting investigations in the Republic of Macedonia? Is that what you want to say?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: What investigations are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Any investigation.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: But it is known who is the president of the country, who is doing what in the ministry. These are things that are known.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said in your statement, concerning what happened to you in the court and in the prison, something. Is it correct, Mr. Bajrami, that you don't know to whom the policemen in the court or the guards in the prison belong and who their superior is, who their chief is?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: In Sutka -- about Sutka, I know. I know who was the police chief, but I don't know who the police chief of the police in the court was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Sutka prison, you knew who the prison commander was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. Zivko was the commander. But I don't know -- only the name I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... know who his commander was, who his superior was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: The chief of whom? Zivko was a director of the prison in -- Sutka prison. This, I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then we'll move on and I'll ask you about things you may have more knowledge of. Is it correct that two months before the events you testified about, because of the conflict with Albanian extremist groups, the army of the Republic of Macedonia took up positions around the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: The Macedonian and -- police and army, yes, they took up positions. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you also aware that on the 10th of August, 2001, in the vicinity of Ljuboten, in Ljubotenski Bacila an extremist Albanian organisation laid a land-mine and eight members of the army were killed and several wounded?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of August, you were at the market in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No. I was in the village. On the 10th of August, I was in Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that because you knew a land-mine had been laid, you and your family went to the basement to take shelter there, for safety; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: That is not correct. It's not correct that we knew, we had information about the mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Bajrami, why, then, were you hiding in the cellars?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: We were hiding because of the shelling which was continuous. That's why we had to take shelter somewhere. We were afraid of the shelling of the Macedonian army. They were firing at the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you, like the other villagers, knew that this was a reaction to the land-mine which had been laid. All the media in Macedonia informed the public of this, so were you aware of it?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No. I don't know who laid any mine. I didn't speak about the land-mine. You asked me -- why we were hiding, and I explained to you that we were hiding because of the continuous shelling. But as to the land-mine, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Bajrami, were the houses in the village grouped by family?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't go to visit other families. I didn't know what the families were doing at that time, whether they were grouped or not. I was looking after my own family. I didn't go to check what the others were doing, because you couldn't go out because of the bullets which were coming in hails.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me clarify. I'm not referring to that day. I'm asking you a general question. Is it true that in the village of Ljuboten the houses were built in such a way that a family - for example, Jusufovski Zendeli and others - lived in a small area in the same neighbourhood. Is that what the situation was in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I explained to you. I didn't go out that day to see what the other families were doing, because there was shelling coming from all sides and the village was surrounded by the police and the army, so I couldn't go out and look at the other families. Ljuboten was, as I said, surrounded by the police and the army and we couldn't go out. We couldn't leave our hiding places or our houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understand very well what you are telling me now, but what you have just told me is not an answer to my question. I would like to ask you to listen carefully and to answer me, if you can. My question was the following: In the village of Ljuboten, do families live in the same neighbourhood, all the brothers and cousins from a single family build their houses next to each other, so that, for example, the Jusufi family lives close to the church, another family lives close to the mosque and so on and so forth. Did you understand me? Is it correct that this is how families live in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. There are families that live together; but there are families which live separately.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bajrami, that the Zendeli family lives close to the cemetery in the village. To be more precise, that family lives on the left side of the road leading from the school towards the cemetery. Is that the area where the Zendeli family lives?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: But there are many Zendeli families. Which one are you asking me about? There isn't a single one by that name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether one of those Zendeli families, if there are several of them, lives not far from the cemetery on the left side of the road leading from the school towards the cemetery, in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. Sulejman lives in the vicinity of the school; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you heard about the shelling in the village on the 10th of August, did you simultaneously learn that three armed persons wearing black uniforms had entered the village?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Which day are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The 10th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit P151.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at this document, Mr. Bajrami, you can see it's an Official Note dated August 2001, and in it one can read that the authorised official who was close to Ljuboten reported that on the road from the school to the cemetery on the left-hand side of the road, towards the Zendeli family houses three persons in black uniforms were observed who were armed with automatic weapons. Would this information perhaps jog your memory, sir, and remind you that on that day three armed persons entered the village?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: There weren't armed people in Ljuboten. This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 21 -- or rather page 21, line 4 where it says August 2001, it should say the 10th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the 10th of August a large number of families left Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: On the 10th of August, 2001, this is what you're asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: It was a Friday, wasn't it? Was it Friday?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Maybe. But I don't know. Maybe it is true, but I can't tell you for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the 10th to the 12th, as you testified, you were at home?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Ahmeti house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Adem Ametovski, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, were you in the house all the time, or did you go out from time to time and observe the situation?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I stayed in the house. I couldn't leave the house because of the shelling and the bullets that came like they were a hail. The village was surrounded by all sides. It was impossible to leave. They shot from Malisten, Ljubance, Rastak, from our mountain, the army fired or shelled the village and fired their arms at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bajrami, that in the basement in which you were, there were boxes next to the door so that one could not leave the basement. They were there for safety.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: We were in the basement, and the police asked us to leave the house through the window. The door was not closed or locked or anything. The police asked to us leave through the window.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You say that if someone were to testify before this Court that the door was secured with crates for your safety that that person would not be telling the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean "with crates."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Boxes, crates. Was the door barricaded with such things or not?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I know that there were boxes with clothes. But the door was not blocked. It was not blocked.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You say you did not leave the cellar from the 10th to the 12th of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now previously move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Bajrami, and correct, that you personally did not go to the new house or to other parts of the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown 65 ter 1396 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 1D96, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 1D0430. Page 1D0430.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were the son of Aziz; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement your father gave to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal, in point 30 he says: "Like I said before [In English] Nevaip was in the new house and Vebi were going back and forth. Because of this and the time I can't really say anymore the precise flow of the movement. At the end Vebi and Mevludin went also to Adem's basement." [Interpretation] Do you agree with me, Mr. Bajrami, that your father's statement differs from what you have just said?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I didn't go out of the basement to walk over the streets of the neighbourhood. I am telling you that we stayed in Adem's basement on the 10th and 11th. I didn't go out to visit the village. I remained in the basement of Adem's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown in this same document pages 1D0428 and 1D0429 simultaneously. Your Honours, as these are statements which we have only in English, I am reading this part of the statement as best I can so that the interpreters can interpret this to the witness into Albanian. Could we have -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your father also said the following, the last sentence on page 0428 says: "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... New house is the neighbour house of [Interpretation] doesn't say who. [In English] In 2001 the new house was nearly finished. Xhelal was working in this house. The house was not really occupied. It was only used by the young people if they wanted, but in 2001 Xhelal normally slept regularly in the old house. In the night from Tuesday, 9 August, to Friday, 10 August Xhelal slept with his cousin, Kadri and Bajram Jashari. Also my son Nevaip was in the new house. Later on Sunday I saw Nevaip in the basement of Adem. I don't know when Nevaip went there. My son Vebi and Mevludin, they were going back and forth between the old where we were hiding and the small barn in the new house." [Interpretation] Is it correct, Mr. Bajrami, that this part of your father's statement differs from what you said in your testimony before this Court?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: As Vebi, I disagree with that. What my father has stated, let him state. I'm telling you where I was. I didn't go out of the basement to -- to walk on the streets of the village. I'm here today and I'm telling you what I saw that day. I cannot tell you what I didn't see. He's my father. Let him tell you what he saw. I want to abide by my statement. I want to tell you what I went through and what I saw, what I eye-witnessed. As to Nevaip and others, I don't want to speak about that. Whoever is here to testify to what he has seen with his own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I would now like to ask you some questions about other matters you mentioned in your statement to the Prosecutor in the statement admitted into evidence today. When the describing the death of your brother Sulejman, you said that you heard a conversation between Sulejman and one of the persons in uniform before he was hit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: That is correct. When they asked us to leave the basement, the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move back into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to suggest to you, Mr. Bajrami, that the real truth is actually that your brother was killed when he tried to escape, would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know that he tried to escape. I didn't see him attempting to escape. They beat my brother. Then we heard the shots. When they asked us to get up to take to Ljubanci, then I saw my brother was killed. And my brother told them "Don't beat me, because I was injured when I was serving in the Macedonian army" and then they said to him, "We will give you a pension for that and we will cure you." Then we saw my brother dead on the way to Ljubanci, when we were going towards Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All that you said was already told in your statement to the Prosecutor. In that statement you also said that only your ID was taken from you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Did you say in your statement that only your ID was taken from you. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Not the passport. A certificate. My wrist-watch, they were about to break my arm when trying to rob me of my wrist. But not the passport, the identity card. And the tobacco and, as I said, the wrist-watch.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was taken away from Mevludin?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know about Mevludin. But they took a lot of money from my brother Nevaip and from my father and from Adem and the others. I personally didn't have any money on me. I told you what they took away from me, but they took away a lot of money from my father and my brother and the wife of my brother, my mother as well. They got a lot of money from us and looted a lot of stuff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, Mr. Bajrami is that correct that while walking by the Macedonian houses in the village of Ljuboten some of the civilians also attacked you and that you noticed a woman shouting at you?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, it wasn't the civilians who beat us, but the uniformed policemen. The woman who was shouting, I don't know her last name. And she said, "Why haven't you killed all of them, you motherfuckers," and then they started beating us even more after those words.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, is it true that your brothers Rafiz and Shefajet were the members of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No. In 2001 Rafiz Bajrami was in Italy, and the other was in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that Shefajet was a member of the -- of Commander Teli's group?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No. I don't know that. I know that he was in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that Rafiz was a member of the 114th NLA Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I knew that he was in Italy.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the beginning of August a -- Commander Teli's group was discovered in Skopje and that in the clashes Commander Teli died because of what commander Arusha decided to retaliate to the army and the police. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't a member of that group as you are saying. I was a farmer. I minded my own business. I worked all day, and I explained to you what happened to us when the police came. I was taking care of my sheep and cattle and I didn't care about Commander Teli or anything like that. I had nothing to do with such people as you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that your brother Shefajet, called Shef, participated in the planting of the mine in Ljubotenski Bacila after which he entered the village?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask to move to a private session now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know Kenan Salievski, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. As one of our villagers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, he was the crisis committee president in the village. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't be precise. I heard something about that. It may be true, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kenan Salievski was the person who later informed you about the arrival of the ICTY investigators and used to call you to go and talk with them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't understand. What investigators are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the Prosecutors of this Tribunal used to come to Skopje or to Ljuboten, Mr. Salievski was the one who was informing you when you were supposed to go and give a statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know. I may have been forgotten after what I went through. We were greatly maltreated, as I said. I still feel pains to this day. I don't remember that. Maybe it's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be now shown 65 ter 1D85, page 1D1193.40, 4-0.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement that he gave to the ICTY investigators on the 6th of November, 2004 and 7th of November, 2004, Mr. Salievski said, being asked: "[In English] ... they are members of NLA. I say that Suad Saliu, Riza Januzi, Besim Murtezani, Rafiz Bajrami, Shefajet Bajrami, Fikret Aliu, Nimet Aliu, Ruhan Jashari or Bajrami, Ramadan Alimi, killed in Matejce mountains; Musa Selimi, Refedin Selimi, Faik Murati, Shefket Murati, Zekir Murati, and Rasim Murati. I think they were about 18 people, but I don't remember all names." [Interpretation] Mr. Bajrami, the statement of Mr. Kenan Salievski is different than yours in respect to your brother's participation in the NLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: They are different, but it is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement and also today, answering the questions of my learned colleague the Prosecutor, you have said that you were brought in the court in Skopje whereby you gave a statement to the investigating judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: What are you saying? What are you -- I don't understand. Can you explicitly state from the court where it took me?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague showed you some documents and you confirm -- you confirm that from the Mirkovci police station you were taken to the Basic Court II in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also shown your statement that you gave before the investigating judge in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, but they put the words differently. They added more words compared to what I said, and they didn't tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, I'll ask you to look into Prosecutor's Exhibit P248. My learned colleague showed you this Official Note of the Mirkovci police station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You do not know Angel Petkovski who signed this Official Note, do you?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All you know in respect to this note is that the other four persons together with you were brought to the court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, all of us who were in Mirkovci were sent to the court, with the exception of three others who went to Bulnic [phoen]. We went to the court, we others.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask that you are shown Prosecution Exhibit P46 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We recognise that we need to interrupt you. We must have the first break at this point, and we'll resume at five minutes past --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I have a rather urgent matter to convey to the Court. Perhaps the witness can be excused. It will only take a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We're going to have the first morning break now, and the court officer will take you outside now and we'll start again at five past 11.00. So if could you go with the court officer now, Mr. Bajrami. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next two witnesses scheduled to testify are Mr. Sulejman Zendeli and then a protected witness, M053. I received notification about 40 minutes ago that Mr. Zendeli had to receive treatment for an ear infection over the weekend and he is not fit enough to testify today. Therefore, if we were to follow the schedule, after the present witness finishes, the next witness would be Witness M053. And I would like -- I wanted to notify the Chamber of this slight predicament. And perhaps if the Prosecution and Defence counsel could speak about this during the break, I just don't know if the Defence counsel are prepared for the start of M53's evidence today or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now and counsel might confer about the situation. Perhaps, Ms. Residovic, can you indicate how much longer you would expect to be with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, very short. Not more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Apostolski -- Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I think I will have around 45 minutes to one hour for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. That will give you and all counsel some indication of the process. The Chamber can't imagine that this witness will go beyond the next break, if I could indicate, Mr. Saxon, so there will certainly be the last session. But if you could all discuss that matter and we will learn the outcome when we resume. When we resume will now be more 10 past than five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, before the break we spoke about the fact that you were taken from the Mirkovci police station to the Basic Court in Skopje and that there you were interviewed by the investigating judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Some of them are correct, some not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were brought before the investigating judge, you said that you were indigent and then the Court appointed an ex officio defence counsel for you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as it says in this record, Ljubisa Dimitrov was appointed your defence counsel. He was there when you were interviewed. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness again be shown document P46, page 66 in English and page 65 in Macedonian. I do apologise. I'm using the document shown to the witness by the Prosecutor, and in English the number is ET-0463-8837-0463-8839. This is then page 4 in this document in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just to assist my learned colleague, we have the hard copy because it's quite illegible in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that could help Ms. Residovic quite a bit. A hard copy is available for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you very much. I think that this page, which we have on e-court now, does not show what we have in our hard copy. So I will ask for the pages I mentioned previously in e-court. It may be simplest to show the page just shown to the witness by the Prosecutor. Your Honours, I do apologise. As the Macedonian text is not very legible, and this morning the Prosecutor supplied with us a hard copy to make things easier, probably, but the hard copy does not totally correspond to what is in e-court so it's the first page. Could we now see the third page, please? Yes, page 3 in English. Yes, where it says "Bajrami Nevaip is my brother." And in Macedonian it's probably also -- or, rather, in Macedonian it's page 2, not page 3. It's the last paragraph on page 2 of the text in Macedonian. Thank you. And I apologise for this brief delay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, first of all, is it correct that you know the members of the Ramadani family?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, I know them. They were together with me. We were together in the court as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Beqir Ramadani, Osman Ramadani and Ismail Ramadani are brothers, and they are all the sons of Muharem Ramadani; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to take a look at the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the last paragraph in Macedonian, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, sorry to interrupt, but I would like to clarify the documents were exactly the same. I simply, for the purpose of speeding up, I put the paragraph number in both English and Macedonian. But the documents are the same, the ones that are in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So please look at the last paragraph on the screen and would the witness in his hard copy, look at the part marked 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I fully agree with my learned friend that it's the same text, but the text that the witness has is marked with these numbers, which makes it easier for the witness to find his way around the document. As the last paragraph in the Macedonian version is marked 10, could it be zoomed in on a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, the Macedonian text is not very legible, but I will try to read what I see in Macedonian. It reads here that, "Nevaip Bajrami is my brother." Is that correct? Is he your brother?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it goes on to say: "As far as I understood, he was transferred to the hospital. I don't know which hospital." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ismail Ramadani, who is my neighbour, was also in hospital. "Beqir Ramadani," it says here, "is my brother." It's an obvious mistake.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Beqir Ramadani is not my brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is his brother. But it says here --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. So Beqir Ramadani is part -- is a brother of Ismail Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As is Osman Ramadani, is that correct, who are my neighbours?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: They are brothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they are your neighbours. And you see here behind the name of Beqir Ramadani there is the word "mi," instead of -- M-I instead of M-U, which in Macedonian --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: This is interpreter's comment -- would be -- is "my brother" instead of is "his brother."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it is clearly seen here that there was a typo regarding one of the letters. Do you see that? So these three persons, Beqir Ramadani, Osman Ramadani, Ismail Ramadani, are brothers and they are your neighbours. Is that what you stated to the judge?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I haven't told the judge that they are my brothers. This is what the Court wrote. I did not tell them that they are my brothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I'm not asking you whether you stated this because you couldn't have stated that. But is it correct that it is written here that, Ismail Ramadani, who is my neighbour, is also in the hospital; Beqir Ramadani, and it is M-I, instead of M-U, "my" instead of "his" brother, as well as Osman Ramadani; and that those persons, Ismail, Beqir and Osman are your neighbours. Is that what you stated to the judge, they are brothers and your neighbours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Would you be kind to turn to the following page in the Macedonian text. The distinguished judge asked you whether you also stated that the civilians beat you up. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Can you specify where were we beaten up? Can you tell me exactly what you're talking?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When my learned colleague asked but this statement, the distinguished president of the Trial Chamber also asked you whether you were beaten by civilians and you stated that you were not. Was it so, as far as I remember, I could not quote the words from the transcript because I don't see them now. But is it correct that you responded that the civilians did not beat you? I apologise, I --

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: We were beaten up only by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That the judge did not ask the question but I thought that His Honour asked the question. If it not the case, then the mistake mine. But I will then ask you a direct question, considering that on the page 3, line 6, there are the words: "We were all beaten by the local population while we were walking down the road." Did you state this before the judge and is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, it is not true. I have said that we were beaten up only by the police, not by the civilians. What you said is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were released from detention after the president pardoned you, is it correct that you did not go and report the persons who had beaten you in Ljuboten, in the police station, in the court, and in the prison?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: You're asking me about the time when I was released from prison, yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Is it correct that you did not go and report any of the persons who have beaten you?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I could not do that, because they would give me more beating. They beat you without any reason. There was no reason for me to go there to report it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So up until the present day, you did not want to talk things out with the Macedonian police or any other Macedonian bodies at all, regarding the events that took place?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: These were exactly the people who beat me. How can you go to the same people to talk to them about beating? There was no reason for me to go there. They were the same people who beat us. They were the law themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never asked your attorney to go and file a report on your behalf against those persons who have beaten you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: What counsel, what attorney are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Any attorney. In Skopje, there are many attorneys. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You never went to an attorney and asked him to file a report on your behalf against the persons who have beaten you up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I went to an Albanian attorney. I told him what had happened. He was an Albanian attorney.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did an attorney ever file a report on your behalf? Did you ever request an attorney to do that?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No. I talked to this attorney, but he has done nothing so far.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, tell me, is it correct that you described the events only to representatives of international organisations and to the investigators of this Tribunal and that you felt this was sufficient and for this reason you did not turn to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: This is correct. I could not tell anything to the Macedonian side because they might have disappear me. We have talked only to The Hague Tribunal. I could not talk to the Macedonian side because, probably, they would simply make a disappear.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, have I completed my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. Now, Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajrami, good morning.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Jasmina Zivkovic and together with my colleague Mr. Antonio Apostolski, I appear for Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Mr. Bajrami, my learned friends from the Prosecution and my colleague from the Defence, Ms. Residovic, put questions to you and you told them that you had made two statements up to now. Before you came to testify before this Tribunal today, did you again read the statements you made to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal, and does the content of those statements represent, to the best of your recollection, the events in Ljuboten as you experienced them on the 10th and 12th of August? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. I know really what happened. I never forget them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bajrami, you are a farmer by profession and that has always been your occupation, as far as I understand?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, farmer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You completed primary school in your mother tongue, and that is the whole extent of your education? I don't know whether you heard my question. Is that the whole extent of your education?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. I have finished the 8th grade school.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever try to find any other job?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No. No, I could not. Nobody accept you. You may want, but they do not accept you. Where can you go?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Who did not accept you?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I have not made any attempt for a job, but it was clear that you could not get a job.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you clarify why it was clear?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: It was clear because I had only 8th grade education. I had no secondary education. I had no university education. I had only 8th grade education, so that was clear, it was not easy for me to get a job.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Said you served in the army. Can you tell what branch of the armed services you served in?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: In Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but what branch.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Pesadi [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Infantry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, in your statement of the 8th of February, 2003, 2D00236 - now it's P247.1 - you said that during the events in Ljuboten you were beaten by members of the security forces and that you suffered numerous injuries. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: That is correct. I have still pains. They came into the house. It is correct what you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that because of your injuries, you are still experiencing health problems, especially with your memory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. I have still health problems. I have still pains.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: As you stated, from the 10th to the 12th of August, 2001, you were in Adem Ametovski's house. You repeated that here today. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And your other brothers were in this house as well, right?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your parents were there, three of your brothers --

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: My parents were at the neighbours' house. They were there because our room was not enough for them. They were there with my mother and with the wives of my brothers. Here in this house it was me and my brothers and my cousins and my friends.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Three brothers from the Ramadani family; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And three brothers from the Ametovski family?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And you all went to that cellar from your houses because that cellar was safer, it was more secure. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, on Friday, the 10th of August, 2001, the shooting in the village began at around 8.00 a.m.; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The shooting came from Malisheva.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Malistena? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, Malisten. They came from there. Shooting came also from the church of Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And that was shelling and firing from light infantry weapons, if I understood your statement correctly?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: That's normal there from the church. There was -- there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And this went on until 2.00 p.m. on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly because we could not look at the clock. I'm not convinced about the exact time, but shooting continued for a long time. There was no interruption.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On Saturday, the 11th of August, shooting and shelling was also heard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You were still in the Ademovski -- or, rather, Adem Ametovski cellar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You remained there throughout this time until the members of the security forces forced you outside on Sunday, the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the -- yes, the Macedonian forces took us, took us out of the basement through the window.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So to confirm again, you were in that cellar throughout these three days and you did not leave the cellar nor did your brothers leave it?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. We only went to the lavatory.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move briefly move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, today my learned friend from the Prosecution gave us a folder containing some documents, including tab 3. That's P48, pages 64 to 68 -- to 66, excuse me. In paragraph 10, or, rather, 11 in the English version, in your statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether we can see this now. This is P46.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: This is your statement made to the investigating judge. It's page -- page 3. Page 3. And paragraph 11 is marked here. Do you see the Macedonian version before you now on the right-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes. But I cannot see it well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's a poor photocopy. I will read to you. You say: "It was Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001, around noon. I was sitting together with," and then there's a part that's illegible, "and wife. We were in our two rooms and we could hear detonations, shots, but I didn't know who was shooting. Suddenly, the police entered our house. At that time, we were still in the our rooms. They fired shots above our heads and several policemen entered our yard. They started a search. They even searched our old house, and because I was frightened, we went to our neighbour's house, Medzit and Zija Ametovski's house." Mr. Bajrami, it's clear from this statement of yours that you were not in the Ametovski house, as you say, from Friday until Sunday. It's clear from this statement that on Sunday, you were still in your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: That is not true. On Sunday, I was in the house of Ametovski. I was in the basement. It is not correct to say that I was in my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: This means that what I have just read out, that you didn't state that in fact?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajrami, is it true and correct that Rafiz and Shefajet are your brothers and at the time of these events they were in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, they were not in Ljuboten. As I told you three or four times, Rafiz was in Italy; Shefajet was in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And let's clarify once more. My learned colleague asked you with regards to the land-mine laying at Ljubotenski Bacila, you stated that you did not know about it. Does it mean that you never heard about that event or that you did not who placed the mine there?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I do not know anything about that event. Only afterwards I saw it on television about it. But before that I do not know anything about it, who put it. But then I was at the prison, and afterward I saw on television and learned about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bajrami, do you know who is Commander Miskoja?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: It means that you don't know that he and his troops tried to enter the village of Ljuboten on Sunday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: There has been no commander in Ljuboten, no commander at all. There has been no commander in the village of Ljuboten. The Macedonian forces were there. The village was encircled. Racak, they were all -- Radishan they were all police points. The whole village of Ljuboten was encircled by army and the police. How can a commander get into the village?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But is then correct that NLA shelled the members of the security forces with mortars from the Pop Cesme locality?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know about Pop Cesme. We are talking about Ljuboten. I was not there. I'm only talking about Ljuboten. In Ljuboten there was no UCK -- there was no person of UCK in Ljuboten. There were only civilians in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Right. But as you stated before, there were check-points everywhere of the police and of the army and I assume that you know that those positions of the army was stationed there because of the frequent attacks of NLA against the neighbouring villages, precisely because of that, because of those terrorists attacks?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: No. The army and the police of Macedonia came to the village one month before. They set up an encirclement one month before the village was placed under siege by the army and the police. We were farmers. We were working in the fields. We had livestock. They did not allow us to take livestock to pastures. So we could see them. We saw how the whole village was encircled by the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bajrami, so you have stated definitely today that you were in the Ametovski's basement and that you hid there because of the shots taking place on the 10th and the 11th of August, but as you are saying, you still remained in that basement on the 12th of August, the Sunday, although there was no shooting then on that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And why were you in the basement if there was no shooting on the 12th of August, on Sunday?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: Where could I go? The police -- the army was there. Where could I go? I had nowhere to go. They beat up people. They killed people. So I went to the basement. There was nowhere I could go. This is what I could do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Right. But my question is the following: You now confirm before his -- Their Honours that on the Sunday, the 12th, there was no shooting, there was no shelling in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
utterances.text: I don't know very well, but there was no reason for the infantry to enter Ljuboten. They entered the village, they went into the houses, they beat up as they wished. They took us in the streets --

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Mr. Bajrami, could you just answer my question? Was there shooting and shelling or not on the 12th of August, Sunday?

utterances.speaker: VEHBI BAJRAMI
